canonical_statement: Every centered variance-one real probability law with a two-sided exponential moment admits a common-space coupling of iid variables with that law and iid standard Gaussian variables whose partial-sum discrepancy through every positive n has an exponentially decaying tail above C log n + x, with positive law-dependent constants C, K, and lambda.
domain_and_universes: mu : Measure Real; existential Omega : Type with MeasurableSpace Omega; P : Measure Omega; X Y : Nat -> Omega -> Real; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: the identity and square are integrable under mu
mu has mean zero and second moment one
there is delta > 0 for which exp(delta * abs x) is integrable
conclusion: There is a probability-space coupling of iid mu increments X and iid N(0,1) increments Y, and positive C, K, lambda, such that P(max_{1 <= k <= n} abs(sum_{i<k} X_i - sum_{i<k} Y_i) > C log n + x) <= ofReal(K exp(-lambda x)) for every n >= 1 and x >= 0.

degenerate_cases: The input is normalized to variance one, so zero variance is excluded explicitly by the second-moment equation. n starts at one; x may be zero. The n=1 event is kernel-checked to equal the first-increment discrepancy. Gaussian input laws are not excluded.
